title: Mercury sessions and the song Bald Head
summary: He cannot say who supervised the Mercury sessions or where they were cut; he explains Bald Head came from a girlfriend with no hair.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, I know. I know. It's a dew drop. The dew drop doesn't look like it used to in the old days. No. No. Dew drop's the same one. So after that, all right, when did you do- you said the Atlantic was the- no, not the Atlantic, the Star Talent was the first record. Mm-hmm. And then you went with Mercury. Yeah. Okay, do you remember who supervised those Mercury sessions? Who did that? Do you remember who got him?

No, Mr. William B. Allen was handling the whole situation at that time. So you think- I never did handle the business part of it. You can't- Was he in the studio when you did that? I just remember where. I'm sure he was. He had to be there, you know what I mean, because he was handling the business part of the situation.
That- was- did you do these at Cosmos on Rampart Street?
No, I don't think so. I think these were- did some building on Canal Street. I don't know whether it was- Bessau Blanc or Gacho- Gacho-
I think so, yeah. Oh, now there was a studio in the Gacho building. Yeah. I know there was.

It was my idea to carry as much business as I could to Cosmo because I figured he would look out for my interests if I helped him with his, you know. Right. So all the talent and everything that I was scouting, I would bring it to the J&M studio.

What you do remember was on the- yeah, I'm trying to- there was a man who had a studio in the Gacho building. It wasn't the most popular studio. I'm trying to think who he was. Come on, Quint. Turn the lights back on, please. No, there was a man who had a studio. He says that the- uh, Mercury- first Mercury stuff was done in the Gacho building. I'm trying to remember the man's name of the studio. And I can't think of it, but I've got it at home. And I'll remember it later on. So you did- Mercury did Bald Head. Now you told me Bald Head was about somebody. She- My little girlfriend I used to- The girl? Yeah.

Come to see me one night, and all the fellas looked up and saw her coming at the door. And they all- oh, look at that. And I knew what they was talking about. Yeah, you ain't got no hair. That's where she chewed a pop bottle at me. Took a long time to understand that the song was going to be popular. Well, if it started getting popular, she got along with it very well.
